newsitem.title: RWANDA: Irish president urges help for African peace search.
newsitem.headline: Irish president urges help for African peace search.

text.p: The international community should support African efforts to solve problems of the Great Lakes region, Irish President Mary Robinson told a conference on Sunday.
Her speech came against unrest in Rwanda, Burundi and Sudan and a background of deepening crisis in eastern Zaire where rebels now control a strip of territory over 1,000 km (600 miles) long.
Robinson, who was the first head of state to visit Rwanda after the 1994 genocide in which 800,000 ethnic Tutsis and allied Hutus died, was later to visit Irish aid workers.
In a speech that ranged from the role of women in Africa to the need for new forms of diplomacy to head off conflicts, she proposed an international conference on peace, security and development.
Such a conference, she said, could be held under the auspices of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity to seek a resolution of the problems of the Great Lakes region.

The Kigali conference, organised by Rwandan women under the auspices of the Rwandan government, the OAU and the Economic Commission for Africa, is to end on Monday. It is discussing the resolution of conflict and promoting peace and development in Africa.

"In my view, poverty is the worst enemy to global peace at the end of this century," she said. "The people of Africa are surely entitled to look to the international community for generous support and assistance at this time of transition."
Respect for human rights, she said, was essential for peace and the world should assume collective responsibility to deter, anticipate, prevent and terminate violations.
